title: Three fungi in a college laboratory
body: A student examined three fungi in the college laboratory and noted the following. Fungus X grew on stale bread. Its mycelium had no cross walls and many nuclei lay in a continuous cytoplasm. Asexual spores were formed inside a sporangium, and when two compatible strains met, a thick-walled zygospore formed from the fusion of two gametes. Fungus Y appeared as a mould on rotting fruit. Its mycelium was branched and had cross walls. Chains of spores were produced at the tips of special hyphae, outside any sac, and in sexual reproduction spores were produced inside sac-like structures grouped in a fruiting body. Fungus Z was an umbrella-shaped growth on a damp log. Its mycelium was branched and septate, no asexual spores were seen, and sex organs were absent. Two somatic cells of different strains fused, and later four spores developed on the outside of a club-shaped cell in the gills of the fruiting body.
